# Overview

This file is the single place where **all** datasets consumed by the rapid app
are prepped and written. Every object written here lands in the app repo, `../nps_wsva_app/app_data/`.

| Output | Contents |
|-------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| `final_indicators.csv` | One row per water supply, one column per indicator (raw values) |
| `water_supplies.csv` | Water supply attributes + state water rights doctrine |
| `wbm_data.gpkg` | LOCA2 climate change summary, spatialized |
| `municipal_hauled.gpkg` | Municipal / hauled / tribal / purchased supplies |

Indicator values are written as **raw** (un-normalized) values. The app
re-normalizes and aggregates them on the fly via `calc_vulnerability_index()`,
so normalization must stay out of this file.

**Index hierarchy (calculated in the app, not here):** Indicators to Vulnerability
Factors to Components (Exposure / Sensitivity) to Total Vulnerability Index,
following the Euclidean distance framework of
[Michalak et al. (2021)](https://irma.nps.gov/DataStore/Reference/Profile/2287636).

# 0. Paths and helpers

```{r paths-helpers}
# All paths are relative to project root (set in the setup chunk)
dir_out <- "data/rapid/outputs"   # date-stamped indicator outputs
dir_app <- "../nps_wsva_app/app_data"   # what the app reads (a clone of nps_wsva_app next to this repo)
dir_int <- "data/rapid"           # intermediate / archive products

dir.create(dir_app, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)


#' Most recent date-stamped file for a given stem
#'
#' Matches `<stem>_YYYY-MM-DD.<ext>` anchored at both ends, so files with extra
#' leading or trailing text (e.g. `kw_runoff_exposure_...`,
#' `..._moderate_...`) are excluded automatically.
#'
#' @param stem file name stem, e.g. "runoff_exposure"
#' @param dir directory to search
#' @param ext file extension, without the dot
#' @return full path to the most recent match, or NA_character_ if none
latest_file <- function(stem, dir = dir_out, ext = "csv") {
  files <- list.files(
    dir,
    pattern = paste0("^", stem, "_\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}\\.", ext, "$"),
    full.names = TRUE
  )
  if (length(files) == 0) return(NA_character_)
  dates <- as.Date(str_extract(basename(files), "\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}"))
  files[which.max(dates)]
}
```

# 1. Indicator registry

**This tibble is the only place to edit when an indicator is added, renamed, or
retired.** Everything downstream (which files get read, which columns get kept,
what they are called in the app, and the column order of
`final_indicators.csv`) is derived from it.

To add a new indicator:

1.  Add a row below with the app-facing name, the raw column name in the output
    file, and the file stem.
2.  Knit. The validation chunk reports anything that did not land.
3.  Add a matching row to `app_data/indicator_details.csv` in `nps_wsva_app` (label,
    description, direction, status) and to `indicator_config` in `app.R`.

Conventions:

-   `app_name` prefix is `exp_` (Exposure) or `sen_` (Sensitivity).
-   `source_col` is always a `raw_` column. Do not register `norm_` columns.
-   Model-agreement columns must be **fraction scale (0-1)**, not percent, or
    they will swamp the amount indicators during aggregation.
-   For multi-metric outputs, pick the percentile that is most vulnerable:
    `p10` for runoff / precip / SWE / drought (largest decrease), `p90` for
    everything else (largest increase).

```{r indicator-registry}
indicator_registry <- tribble(
  ~app_name,                              ~source_col,                                    ~file_stem,                            ~component,    ~factor,

  # ---- EXPOSURE ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Runoff
  "exp_runoff_change",                    "raw_runoff_change_p10",                        "runoff_exposure",                     "Exposure",    "Runoff",
  "exp_runoff_model_agree",               "raw_runoff_models_showing_decrease",           "runoff_exposure",                     "Exposure",    "Runoff",
  "exp_runoff_timing_change",             "raw_runoff_timing_change_magnitude",           "runoff_timing_exposure",              "Exposure",    "Timing",
  "exp_runoff_timing_change_model_agree", "raw_runoff_timing_direction_agreement_fraction","runoff_timing_exposure",             "Exposure",    "Timing",

  # Precipitation
  "exp_precip_change",                    "raw_precipitation_change_p10",                 "precipitation_exposure",              "Exposure",    "Precipitation",
  "exp_precip_model_agree",               "raw_precip_models_showing_decrease",           "precipitation_exposure",              "Exposure",    "Precipitation",
  "exp_precip_timing_change",             "raw_precip_timing_change_magnitude",           "precip_timing_exposure",              "Exposure",    "Timing",
  "exp_precip_timing_change_model_agree", "raw_precip_timing_direction_agreement_fraction","precip_timing_exposure",             "Exposure",    "Timing",

  # Temperature
  "exp_temp_change",                      "raw_temperature_change_p90",                   "temperature_exposure",                "Exposure",    "Temperature",

  # Drought (negative SPEI change = drier = more vulnerable)
  "exp_drought_change",                   "raw_spei_change_p10",                          "drought_exposure",                    "Exposure",    "Drought",
  "exp_drought_model_agree",              "raw_spei_models_showing_decrease",             "drought_exposure",                    "Exposure",    "Drought",

  # Sea level rise
  "exp_inundation_slr",                   "raw_pct_point_change",                         "inundation_exposure",                 "Exposure",    "Sea Level Rise",
  "exp_swi",                              "raw_swi_migration",                            "swi_exposure",                        "Exposure",    "Sea Level Rise",
  "exp_storm_surge",                      "raw_surge_change_max",                         "storm_surge_exposure",                "Exposure",    "Sea Level Rise",

  # Fire
  "exp_fire_prob_change",                 "raw_fire_prob_change_p90",                     "fire_exposure",                       "Exposure",    "Wildfire",
  "exp_fire_model_agree",                 "raw_fire_models_showing_increase",             "fire_exposure",                       "Exposure",    "Wildfire",

  # Demand
  "exp_nearby_use_change",                "raw_use_change_p90",                           "nearby_use_exposure",                 "Exposure",    "Demand",
  "exp_nearby_use_model_agree",           "raw_models_showing_increase_pct",              "nearby_use_exposure",                 "Exposure",    "Demand",
  "exp_auc_change",                       "raw_timing_change_p90",                        "timing_mismatch_exposure_Pred_High",  "Exposure",    "Demand",

  # ---- SENSITIVITY ---------------------------------------------------------
  # Demand
  "sen_visitation_trend",                 "raw_scaled_trend_visitation",                  "visitation_sensitivity",              "Sensitivity", "Demand",
  "sen_competition",                      "raw_slope_nearby_use_per_km2",                 "nearby_use_sensitivity",              "Sensitivity", "Demand",
  "sen_auc_change",                       "raw_timing_mismatch_auc",                      "timing_mismatch_sensitivity",         "Sensitivity", "Demand",

  # Infrastructure
  "sen_source_type",                      "raw_groundwater_depth_m",                      "groundwater_depth_sensitivity",       "Sensitivity", "Infrastructure",

  # Hydro-climate trends
  "sen_runoff_trend",                     "raw_slope_runoff",                             "runoff_sensitivity",                  "Sensitivity", "Runoff",
  "sen_precip_trend",                     "raw_slope_precip",                             "precip_sensitivity",                  "Sensitivity", "Precipitation",
  "sen_drought_trend",                    "raw_slope_spei",                               "drought_sensitivity",                 "Sensitivity", "Drought",
  "sen_temp_trend",                       "raw_slope_temperature",                        "temperature_sensitivity",             "Sensitivity", "Temperature",

  # Hazards
  "sen_wildfire_hazard",                  "raw_wildfire_hazard_mean",                     "fire_sensitivity",                    "Sensitivity", "Wildfire",
  "sen_flood_risk",                       "raw_flood_risk_percent",                       "flood_sensitivity",                   "Sensitivity", "Flood",
  "sen_inundation_current",               "raw_coverage_pct_ref",                         "inundation_exposure",              "Sensitivity", "Sea Level Rise"

  # ---- NOT YET WIRED (uncomment when the output exists) --------------------
  # NOTE: add a trailing comma to the row above before uncommenting any of these
  # "exp_swe_change",       "raw_swe_change_p10",             "swe_exposure",    "Exposure", "Snowpack",
  # "exp_swe_model_agree",  "raw_swe_models_showing_decrease","swe_exposure",    "Exposure", "Snowpack",
  # "exp_flood_change",     "raw_flood_change_p90",           "flood_exposure",  "Exposure", "Flood",
)

# Guard against copy-paste duplicates in the registry itself
stopifnot(
  !anyDuplicated(indicator_registry$app_name),
  !anyDuplicated(indicator_registry$source_col)
)

count(indicator_registry, component, factor)
```

# 2. Assemble indicators

Read the most recent output file for every stem in the registry, keep only the
registered raw columns, and full-join on `wsd_source_id`.

Each file is de-duplicated to one row per `wsd_source_id` **before** joining, so
a duplicated row in any single output cannot fan out the joined table.

```{r read-indicator-files}
indicator_files <- tibble(file_stem = unique(indicator_registry$file_stem)) |>
  mutate(file = map_chr(file_stem, latest_file))

# Report (do not silently drop) stems with no matching output file
missing_files <- filter(indicator_files, is.na(file))
if (nrow(missing_files) > 0) {
  warning("No date-stamped file found for: ",
          paste(missing_files$file_stem, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
}

indicator_files <- filter(indicator_files, !is.na(file))

# Which file / date each indicator is coming from this run
indicator_files |>
  mutate(file_date = str_extract(basename(file), "\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}")) |>
  select(file_stem, file_date) |>
  arrange(file_stem) |>
  print(n = Inf)
```

```{r assemble-indicators}
wanted_cols <- indicator_registry$source_col

indicator_list <- indicator_files$file |>
  set_names(indicator_files$file_stem) |>
  map(\(f) {
    read_csv(f, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
      select(wsd_source_id, any_of(wanted_cols)) |>
      distinct(wsd_source_id, .keep_all = TRUE)
  })

# Fail loudly on cross-file column collisions rather than getting silent .x/.y
col_map <- imap(
  indicator_list,
  \(df, nm) tibble(file_stem = nm, source_col = setdiff(names(df), "wsd_source_id"))
) |>
  list_rbind()

collisions <- col_map |> count(source_col) |> filter(n > 1)
if (nrow(collisions) > 0) {
  stop("Same raw column supplied by more than one file: ",
       paste(collisions$source_col, collapse = ", "),
       ". Rename it upstream in the calc_* script.", call. = FALSE)
}

indicators_assembled <- reduce(indicator_list, full_join, by = "wsd_source_id")

dim(indicators_assembled)
```

## Validation

```{r validate-registry}
# Registry rows that never landed: bad stem, bad column name, or missing file
not_found <- indicator_registry |>
  filter(!source_col %in% names(indicators_assembled)) |>
  select(app_name, source_col, file_stem)

if (nrow(not_found) > 0) {
  warning(nrow(not_found), " registered indicator(s) not found in any output file.",
          call. = FALSE)
  print(not_found)
} else {
  cat("All", nrow(indicator_registry), "registered indicators found.\n")
}

# Confirm the file each column actually came from matches the registry
mismatched_stems <- indicator_registry |>
  inner_join(col_map, by = "source_col", suffix = c("_registry", "_actual")) |>
  filter(file_stem_registry != file_stem_actual) |>
  select(app_name, source_col, file_stem_registry, file_stem_actual)

if (nrow(mismatched_stems) > 0) {
  message("Registry `file_stem` is out of date for these rows (values are still correct):")
  print(mismatched_stems)
}
```

```{r write-assembled}
# Archive copy of the joined raw values, pre-rename
write_csv(indicators_assembled, file.path(dir_int, "indicators_assembled.csv"))
```

# 3. Indicator table for the app

Rename to app-facing names and order columns by the registry. One row per water
supply system.

```{r indicators-clean}
registry_present <- filter(indicator_registry, source_col %in% names(indicators_assembled))

indicators_clean <- indicators_assembled |>
  select(wsd_source_id, all_of(set_names(registry_present$source_col, registry_present$app_name))) |>
  distinct(wsd_source_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

dim(indicators_clean)
```

## Coverage check

```{r indicator-coverage}
# Non-missing count per indicator. A count far below the others usually means a
# genuine data gap, not a bug, but it is worth confirming before the app ingests it.
indicators_clean |>
  summarise(across(-wsd_source_id, ~ sum(!is.na(.x)))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "app_name", values_to = "n_valid") |>
  mutate(pct_valid = round(100 * n_valid / nrow(indicators_clean), 1)) |>
  left_join(select(indicator_registry, app_name, component, factor), by = "app_name") |>
  arrange(n_valid) |>
  print(n = Inf)

# Completeness per supply: how many indicators each site actually contributes.
# NOTE: `na.rm = TRUE` in the app's rowSums() makes a missing indicator and an
# explicit zero mechanically identical, so sites low on this histogram score
# systematically lower. Accepted methodological choice, flagged here for QA.
indicators_clean |>
  mutate(n_indicators = rowSums(!is.na(across(-wsd_source_id)))) |>
  count(n_indicators) |>
  arrange(desc(n_indicators)) |>
  print(n = Inf)
```

```{r write-indicators}
write_csv(indicators_clean, file.path(dir_app, "final_indicators.csv"))
```

# 4. Water supplies

Built here, written at the end of section 5 once the state water rights
attributes have been attached. This is the only write of `water_supplies.csv`.

```{r water-supplies}
water_supplies <- get_wsd(rapid = TRUE) |>
  # some WSDs have NA source_state; fall back to the park-level `state` column
  mutate(source_state = if_else(is.na(source_state), state, source_state)) |>
  distinct(wsd_source_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

dim(water_supplies)
```

# 5. State water rights doctrine

Pulled from `explore_WaterRights_vulnerability.Rmd` (Parts 2a and 3). State
surface water and groundwater appropriation doctrines are joined to each supply
by `source_state` and carried as **descriptive** attributes only. They are not
scored or ranked, and they are not indicators.

The workbook covers CONUS only, so supplies in AK, HI, and the territories will
have `NA` doctrine fields by design.

> **DISCLAIMER (surface as-is in the app):** *The state water rights information
> is intended for general informational purposes only and should not be used as
> an alternative to seeking expert legal advice where necessary. Consult the
> state-specific State Engineer's Office and/or the applicable water resources
> governing body for any legal questions or advice related to water rights
> administration.*

```{r water-rights-state}
water_law <- read_excel("data/all/CONUS States_SW-GW_WaterManagement.xlsx",
                        sheet = "List") |>
  rename(state_name = State)

# Crosswalk state name (used by the workbook) to postal code (used by the WSD)
state_xwalk <- tigris::states(progress_bar = FALSE) |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  select(source_state = STUSPS, state_name = NAME)

water_rights_state <- state_xwalk |>
  inner_join(water_law, by = "state_name") |>
  select(source_state, state_name, SurfaceWaterLaw, GroundWaterLaw,
         any_of("LegalFrameworkRef"))

# Any state in the workbook that failed to match a postal code
setdiff(water_law$state_name, water_rights_state$state_name)
```

```{r join-water-rights}
wr_cols <- setdiff(names(water_rights_state), "source_state")

water_supplies <- water_supplies |>
  select(-any_of(wr_cols)) |>   # keeps the chunk idempotent on re-run
  left_join(water_rights_state, by = "source_state")

# Supplies with no doctrine attached (expect AK / HI / territories only)
water_supplies |>
  filter(is.na(SurfaceWaterLaw)) |>
  count(source_state, sort = TRUE)
```

```{r write-water-supplies}
write_csv(water_supplies, file.path(dir_app, "water_supplies.csv"))
```

# 6. WBM / LOCA2 climate summary

```{r wbm-data}
wbm_file <- latest_file("loca2_climate_change_summary")
stopifnot(!is.na(wbm_file))
cat("Reading:", basename(wbm_file), "\n")

wbm_data <- read_csv(wbm_file, show_col_types = FALSE)

# Supply attributes to carry onto the spatial layer
supply_attrs <- water_supplies |>
  select(any_of(c("wsd_source_id", "park_unit", "park_name", "region",
                  "source_state", "water_system_name", "system_type",
                  "source_type", "source_longitude", "source_latitude")))

wbm_sf <- wbm_data |>
  # drop any duplicated attribute columns so the join cannot produce .x/.y
  select(-any_of(setdiff(names(supply_attrs), "wsd_source_id"))) |>
  left_join(supply_attrs, by = "wsd_source_id") |>
  filter(!is.na(source_longitude), !is.na(source_latitude)) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("source_longitude", "source_latitude"),
           crs = 4326, remove = FALSE)

# Rows that could not be located (no match in the WSD, or missing coordinates)
cat("WBM rows:", nrow(wbm_data),
    "| located:", nrow(wbm_sf),
    "| unique supplies:", n_distinct(wbm_sf$wsd_source_id), "\n")

st_write(wbm_sf, file.path(dir_app, "wbm_data.gpkg"),
         delete_dsn = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)
```

# 7. Municipal / hauled supplies

Full WSD (not the rapid subset), since these system types are excluded from the
scored set but still shown on the map.

```{r municipal-hauled}
municipal_hauled <- get_wsd() |>
  filter(str_detect(source_type,
                    regex("municipal|hauled|tribal|purchased", ignore_case = TRUE))) |>
  distinct(wsd_source_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  filter(!is.na(source_longitude), !is.na(source_latitude)) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("source_longitude", "source_latitude"),
           crs = 4326, remove = FALSE)

st_write(municipal_hauled, file.path(dir_app, "municipal_hauled.gpkg"),
         delete_dsn = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)

nrow(municipal_hauled)
```
